comments.text:
The comment on adults reading and writing - Could be taken as disrespectful. 

Also its SOCA not Soka

replies.author: @RealLifeExplorerUS
replies.text: Our intention was to highlight everyday life in Barbados with respect and appreciation for its people. And you're absolutely right—it’s SOCA, not Soka! We appreciate the correction and will be more careful going forward. Feedback like yours helps us improve and better represent the cultures we explore.

comments.author: @GlobalLifeInsights
comments.text: If your heart doesn't drop a little when the Reggae bus driver starts weaving through traffic while the music is blasting, are you even living?

replies.author: @RealLifeExplorerUS
replies.text: Haha, that's the real Barbados experience! 😂 The music, the energy, and those unexpected turns make it a ride you'll never forget! A little excitement mixed with a little fear, but that's part of the adventure.

comments.author: @stanleygarland5164
comments.text: Why is barbados so much cleaner and in better repair than other Caribbean islands

replies.author: @RealLifeExplorerUS
replies.text: A big part of it comes down to Barbados having a relatively stable economy and a higher GDP per capita, which allows for better investment in infrastructure and public services. Plus, there’s a very strong sense of civic pride among Bajans when it comes to keeping their island beautiful.

comments.author: @mighttactic5580
comments.text: The sea gives Bajans their identity, but climate change is taking a heavy toll on everyday working people.

replies.author: @RealLifeExplorerUS
replies.text: You hit the nail on the head. The connection Bajans have with the ocean is beautiful, but it's heartbreaking to see how environmental changes are impacting the local working class right now.

replies.author: @RealLifeExplorerUS
